newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks slide 2.22 pct on foreign sales.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks slide 2.22 pct on foreign sales.

text.p: Thai stocks slid 2.22 percent on Friday afternoon amid sales by foreigners, facing a severe baht shortage, to raise baht funds and on persistent worries about asset quality of local financial institutions, brokers said.
The index sank 12.16 points to 535.89 at 0748GMT some minutes after the start of the afternoon trading session.

"There were a lot of selling orders from foreigners in the afternoon session," said one dealer at local broker. "Some foreign investment funds now face a shortage of baht. Selling stocks is one way to get the currency."

The baht is trading at a 13-year high against the dollar in offshore forex market as foreign players, in dire need of the Thai unit to cover their short position after mid-May's speculative attack on the currency, dumped dollars to cover short positions.
The central bank has cut off baht supply to foreign speculators after the last speculative attack on the currency.
